adds.title: Missouri Ends Gender-Affirming Care for Transgender Inmates
adds.summary: Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe signed an appropriations law, effective July 2, 2026, that bars any state funds from paying for cross-sex hormones or gender-transition surgery for transgender people in Missouri prisons, with no taper plan for inmates already receiving care. Metro Weekly reports Missouri thereby became the seventh US state, and the second in 2026 after Oklahoma, to ban gender-affirming care for inmates; Florida, Kentucky and North Carolina have near-identical laws, while similar Idaho and Georgia measures were blocked by federal courts. This documents the record's claim that Missouri restricts such treatment for people in prisons and jails.

adds.title: Missouri ban on gender-affirming care for minors upheld by judge
adds.summary: A Missouri judge on November 25, 2024 upheld Senate Bill 49, the 2023 state law prohibiting gender-affirming care for minors; Lambda Legal and the ACLU of Missouri, counsel for the plaintiffs, said they would appeal. CNN reports the law also bars Missouri Medicaid from paying for gender-affirming care for a patient of any age, and that doctors who violate the ban can lose their Missouri medical licence and be sued by patients up to 15 years after treatment. The ruling confirms the care ban the record describes as in force since August 28, 2023.

adds.title: Missouri Supreme Court upholds ban on minor transgender care
adds.summary: The Missouri Supreme Court unanimously upheld the state's ban on gender-transition surgeries, cross-sex hormones and other gender-affirming care for minors on January 13, 2026, quoting the 2025 U.S. Supreme Court ruling that upheld Tennessee's similar ban. STLPR notes the SAFE Act ban enacted in 2023 is set to expire in 2027, that lawmakers want to make it permanent, and that a November 2026 ballot initiative also seeks to ban such care indefinitely. The ruling shows the ban remains enforced and is moving toward permanence rather than being struck down.

adds.title: Families and Medical Providers Sue Missouri to Block Transgender Youth Medical Care Ban
adds.summary: Lambda Legal, the ACLU of Missouri and Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner filed suit on July 25, 2023, in Cole County Circuit Court to block implementation of Missouri's Senate Bill 49, which prevents transgender adolescents from accessing gender-affirming medical care and was scheduled to take effect August 28, 2023. Plaintiffs were three families of transgender young people, medical providers, and PFLAG National and GLMA. The filing documents the effective date of the care ban the record says is in force.

adds.title: Alaska medical board set to vote on restricting treatment of transgender minors
adds.summary: Alaska's State Medical Board, whose members are appointed by Gov. Mike Dunleavy, was set to vote at its August 22, 2025 meeting on formally opposing 'treatment of gender dysphoria in minors' and on a statement opposing late-term abortion, after a board member proposed the resolution in June 2025. The Anchorage Daily News reports Dunleavy's earlier bid to limit transgender students' access to single-sex facilities failed, but a board he appointed limited transgender girls' participation in girls' sports teams. The item documents Alaska's regulatory rather than legislative pressure on transgender care, consistent with the record's moderate-tier 'laws aimed at youth' profile.

adds.title: Mat-Su transgender bathroom ban becomes permanent in apparent first for Alaska
adds.summary: The Matanuska-Susitna Borough School District board in Alaska voted 5-1 on October 19, 2022 to permanently adopt a policy requiring transgender students to use bathrooms matching their sex at birth or a private option such as the nurse's office, overturning guidelines in place for more than seven years. AP reports the policy was described as an apparent first for Alaska. As a school-district policy it is not a state adult facility ban, matching the record's finding that no adult facility ban is recorded for Alaska.

adds.title: Alaska medical board seeks to restrict abortion, transgender medical care
adds.summary: Alaska's health-care regulatory board voted unanimously on August 22, 2025 to recommend restricting medical care for transgender youth and approved a draft regulation that would classify providing gender-transition care to anyone under 18 as 'unprofessional conduct', subject to disciplinary action. The Alaska Beacon story reports the draft regulation must be vetted by the Alaska Department of Law and then undergo a 30-day public comment period. No adult-facility or adult-care ban is involved, consistent with the record's moderate grading for Alaska.

adds.title: Georgia's governor signs ban on certain gender-affirming care for minors
adds.summary: Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp on March 23, 2023 signed Senate Bill 140, barring licensed medical professionals from providing patients under 18 with hormone therapy or surgery related to gender transition, with licence revocation as a possible penalty; minors who began hormone replacement therapy before July 1, 2023 may continue under the law. CNN reports the ACLU of Georgia said it would sue. The ban took effect July 1, 2023, giving an on-the-ground legal restriction relevant to a trans traveller's assessment of Georgia.

adds.title: Georgia agrees to pay for gender-affirming care for public employees
adds.summary: In October 2023 plaintiffs announced a settlement with Georgia's State Health Benefit Plan in Atlanta federal court, requiring the plan to pay for medically necessary gender-affirming care for employees, spouses and dependents, after a December 2022 lawsuit argued the plan illegally discriminated by refusing to pay. The story notes the plan could then be required to pay for care for minors outside Georgia even though prohibited inside the state. This documents that Georgia's public-employee health plan coverage for gender-affirming care continued by settlement despite the 2023 care ban.

adds.title: Atlanta police investigating 3 'violent crimes' against transgender women
adds.summary: Atlanta police said in April 2023 they were actively investigating three 'violent crimes' against transgender women in the city that year, after two Black transgender women were fatally shot a week apart; a January 2023 shooting that left a transgender woman in critical condition also remained open. ABC News quotes the Atlanta Police Department acknowledging the 'epidemic-level violence black and brown transgender women face in America'. The story supports the record's finding that Georgia's documented danger to trans people has been street violence concentrated in Atlanta.

adds.title: Memorial Health halts transgender surgeries: 5 things to know
adds.summary: Memorial Health University Medical Center in Savannah abruptly cancelled all gender-affirming surgeries on February 13, 2025, including a pre-approved double mastectomy for a 24-year-old transgender man, citing a responsibility to follow state and federal laws and regulations that appears to reference the January 28, 2025 federal executive order denying Medicare and Medicaid funding to providers of youth gender-transition care. The Current reports Savannah Pride Center said at least two other area residents were also denied care. This documents on-the-ground shrinkage of adult gender-affirming care access in Georgia under federal funding pressure.

adds.title: Pa. senators passed a transgender female athlete ban. Will the House take it up?
adds.summary: Pennsylvania's Senate on April 22, 2026 passed Senate Bill 1293, the 'Save Women's Sports Act', which would ban transgender female athletes from girls' and women's teams in the commonwealth; the Pennsylvania Capital-Star reports Gov. Josh Shapiro called supportive lawmakers 'extremists', and it was unclear whether the House would take the bill up. The measure targets youth school sports rather than transgender adults or public-facility access. The Senate's action and the governor's opposition frame the state's legal trajectory for a trans visitor.

adds.title: Pennsylvania Governor Vetoes Transgender Sports Ban
adds.summary: Pennsylvania Gov. Tom Wolf on July 11, 2022 vetoed legislation that would have barred transgender athletes from teams matching their gender identity by requiring public K-12 schools and colleges to designate sports as male, female or coed, with athletes in female-designated sports required to have been assigned female at birth. The bill had passed the Republican-led legislature on largely party-line votes. The veto documents Pennsylvania declining to enact an anti-trans measure, matching the record's low-risk grading.

adds.title: Senate Approves 'Save Women's Sports Act' to Protect Fairness in Female Athletics
adds.summary: The Pennsylvania Senate on May 6, 2025 approved Senate Bill 9, the 'Save Women's Sports Act', reserving athletic teams designated for women for 'biological females' in Pennsylvania's K-12 and collegiate sports and sending the bill to the House of Representatives. The press release from the Pennsylvania Senate Republican Caucus, with sponsors including Sens. Judy Ward and Kristin Phillips-Hill, confirms the state Senate has repeatedly backed trans-athlete restrictions for school sports. The measure concerns youth sports participation rather than adult care or public facilities.

adds.title: Human Rights Campaign: Wisconsin Governor Vetoes Bill Targeting Lifesaving Medical Care for Transgender Youth
adds.summary: Wisconsin Gov. Tony Evers on December 6, 2023 vetoed Assembly Bill 465, legislation aimed at restricting health care for transgender youth, according to the Human Rights Campaign, which positioned the veto as keeping the care restriction from taking effect in Wisconsin. The press release quotes HRC's Wisconsin state director welcoming the decision. No gender-affirming-care ban for minors became law in Wisconsin, consistent with the record's low-risk grading of the state's posture toward transgender people.

adds.title: Wisconsin governor vetoes transgender high school athletics ban
adds.summary: Wisconsin Gov. Tony Evers vetoed on April 2, 2024 a bill passed by the Republican-controlled Legislature that would have limited high school athletes to teams matching the gender they were assigned at birth; the bill's sponsor called the veto 'disgusting'. AP reports Evers had promised the veto since the bill was introduced and that Democrats did not have enough votes to stop its passage in the Legislature. The veto documents Wisconsin declining to enact the trans-athlete ban, and the story records no public-facility or adult-care restriction.

adds.title: UW Health, Children's Wisconsin pause gender-affirming care for minors after HHS directive
adds.summary: UW Health and Children's Wisconsin each announced on January 13, 2026 that they would pause gender-affirming pharmacologic care for patients under 18, after the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services said it would deny Medicaid and Medicare payments to hospitals providing such care to minors; WMTV reports Wisconsin Attorney General Josh Kaul had joined a coalition of states to block the HHS declaration. Mental and behavioural health services continued. The pause flows from federal funding pressure on Wisconsin hospitals rather than any state ban.

adds.title: Transgender bill hearings in Wisconsin: What you need to know
adds.summary: Wisconsin Watch reports that October 2023 public hearings in the Wisconsin Legislature on bills to ban gender-affirming care for transgender youth, including the 'Help Not Harm Act' based on model legislation, and to restrict transgender sports participation were marked by misinformation, with lawmaker questions indicating gaps in basic knowledge. The WIAA and NCAA retained their own policies addressing transgender athletes. The piece documents the legislative push against transgender rights in Wisconsin and the absence of enacted bans at the time.
